searchText: Don't link to external tests, inline test cases or add test cases as assets. A better place to collate information would be that HarkMD of yours with all of the links. Inline or asset test cases are ideal, someone just needs to write them. Just a list of inputs and expected outputs, maybe in JSON format or something. <@!333694584607604738> I don't know if this helps, these are the ones I have created for Nethereum https://gist.github.com/juanfranblanco/4cc998247aecd822d6088e382d94a6f1 I am using geth dev to launch a single node clique as per Nethereum example testchains (if that helps for integration testing), i have enabled all the forks at 0 ```json "eip158Block": 0, "byzantiumBlock": 0, "constantinopleBlock": 0, "petersburgBlock": 0, "istanbulBlock": 0, "berlinBlock": 0, "londonBlock": 0, ``` <@!301186049323958275> have you finished that Ethers example to calculate the fees? I believe at the moment we are waiting for the JSON-RPC endpoint to be finalized (see the recent conversation in <#692078615269212180>). In the meantime, my recommendation for *launch day* still remains to just do `2000000000` for the `maxPremiumFeePerGas` and `latestBlock.baseFee * 2 + 2000000000` for the `maxFeePerGas`. It is simple and it should get us smoothly through the launch until we have more data to use to design more complex/competitive strategies. And my recommendation for mining clients is to use `1000000000` as the minimum accepted premium for block inclusion. <@!382487564755402762> oh thanks - this is most helpful! Yeah, I can't help there. Will add the above tests to the mainnet readiness checklist. https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/Fee-Market/mainnet-readiness.md#reference-tests
